topic.name: Calculating Areas of Right Triangles Using Trigonometry

question.text: Given that $\tan(m\angle{A}) = \dfrac{7}{3},$ calculate the area (in square units) of $\triangle ABC$ shown above.
question.explanation:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is \[ \mathcal{A} = \dfrac12 AC \cdot BC. \]

We are given that $\tan(m\angle{A}) = \dfrac{7}{3}.$ Notice that relative to $\angle{A},$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overline{BC}$ and adjacent side $\overline{AC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x{:}$

\begin{align} \tan (m\angle{A}) &=\dfrac{BC}{AC} \\[5pt] \dfrac{7}{3} &= \dfrac{4x-1}{x+1}\\[5pt] 7(x+1) &= 3(4x-1)\\[5pt] 7x+7 & = 12x-3\\[5pt] 7x- 12x & =-3-7\\[5pt] -5x &=-10\\[5pt] x &=2 \end{align}

So, the side lengths are \begin{align*} AC&=x+1 = 2+1 = 3,\\[5pt] BC&=4x-1= 4(2)-1 = 7. \end{align*}

Therefore, the area of $\triangle{ABC}$ is \begin{align} \mathcal A & = \dfrac 1 2 AC\cdot BC \\[5pt] &= \dfrac 1 2 \cdot 3 \cdot 7 \\[5pt] &= 10.5. \end{align}

question.text: Given that $\tan(m\angle{A}) = \dfrac{9}{8},$ calculate the area (in square units) of $\triangle ABC$ shown above.
question.explanation:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is \[ \mathcal{A} = \dfrac12 AC \cdot BC. \]

We are given that $\tan(m\angle{A}) = \dfrac{9}{8}.$ Notice that relative to $\angle{A},$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overline{BC}$ and adjacent side $\overline{AC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x{:}$

\begin{align} \tan(m\angle{A}) &=\dfrac{BC}{AC} \\[5pt] \dfrac{9}{8} &= \dfrac{4x-2}{3x+1}\\[5pt] 9(3x+1) &= 8(4x-2)\\[5pt] 27x+9 & = 32x-16\\[5pt] 9+16 & =32x-27x\\[5pt] 25 &=5x\\[5pt] x &=5 \end{align}

So, the side lengths are \begin{align*} BC&=4x-2 = 4(5)-2 = 18,\\[5pt] AC&=3x+1= 3(5)+1 = 16. \end{align*}

Therefore, the area of $\triangle{ABC}$ is

\begin{align} \mathcal A & = \dfrac 1 2 AC\cdot BC \\[5pt] &= \dfrac 1 2 \cdot 16 \cdot 18 \\[5pt] &= 144. \end{align}

example.title: Finding the Area of a Triangle by Solving for a Variable Given a Trigonometric Ratio of One Angle

question.text: In square units rounded to one decimal place, the area of $\triangle ABC$ is
question.explanation:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is \[ \mathcal{A} = \dfrac12 AC \cdot BC. \]

We are given that $m\angle{B} = 35^\circ.$ Notice that relative to $\angle{B},$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overline{AC}$ and adjacent side $\overline{BC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x{:}$

\begin{align*} \tan (m\angle{B}) &=\dfrac{AC}{BC} \\[5pt] \tan (35^{\circ}) &=\dfrac{x+2}{2x} \\[5pt] {2x}\cdot \tan (35^{\circ}) &= {x+2} \\[5pt] {2x}\cdot \tan (35^{\circ}) - x &= 2 \\[5pt] {x} (2\tan (35^{\circ})-1) &= 2 \\[5pt] x &= \dfrac{2}{ 2\tan (35^{\circ})-1} \\[5pt] x &= 4.994\,8\ldots \end{align*}

So, the side lengths are \begin{align*} BC &= 2x = 2(4.994\,8\ldots)=9.989\,6\ldots, \\[5pt] AC &= x+2 = (4.994\,8\ldots) +2= 6.994\,8\ldots. \end{align*}

Therefore, the area of $\triangle{ABC}$ is \begin{align*} \mathcal A %& = \dfrac 1 2 \cdot AC \cdot BC\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}(9.989\,6\ldots)(6.994\,8\ldots) \\[5pt] &= 34.937\,8\ldots \\[5pt] &\approx \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{34.9}, \end{align*} rounded to one decimal place.
